quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Do not drive in these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more room to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: Which of the following describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no breaks and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to handle them.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all railroad crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must use your turn signal any time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit with caution.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet, which make roads slippery. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit in bad conditions.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter or skateboard riders when the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of low visibility and headlight glare from oncoming cars. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hospital.
Intersection ahead.
Railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and alert drivers to potential hazards ahead. This sign warns you of an upcoming intersection so you can prepare for traffic or turning.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at high speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving on the interstate requires you to stay alert and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without making an emergency stop. An emergency stop can cause the driver behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway:

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must attach a note to it with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, pulling into traffic, and entering or leaving a parking space.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can affect all vehicles.

questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers. It can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust onto the road, and it can physically push vehicles off course.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to all drivers who arrived before you.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait for your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to move back to the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can return to your lane when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spot before moving back.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to police:

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your proof of insurance and license to a police officer whenever requested after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield the right-of-way to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from you.

questions.explanation: Vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
